summary: The Sunshine Protection Act of 2025 makes daylight saving time the permanent standard time across the United States. It repeals the temporary period for daylight saving time under the Uniform Time Act of 1966, advances standard time by one hour across standard time zones, and allows certain states and areas that were previously exempt from daylight saving time to choose either the new permanent daylight saving time or their prior standard time.

affected_groups.effect: They may choose to use either the new permanent standard time or their prior standard time.

affected_groups.effect: Experience daylight saving time as the permanent standard time.
affected_groups.group: General public across the United States

key_provisions: Repeals Section 3 of the Uniform Time Act of 1966.
Advances standard time by adjusting the hour differences from Greenwich Mean Time across the standard time zones.
Permits states and areas that previously exempted themselves from daylight saving time to choose between the new permanent standard time or their prior standard time.
missing_information: The specific effective date for when the permanent change takes effect.
Details on how transportation, commerce, and communication systems will adapt.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Sunshine Protection Act of 2025 makes daylight saving time the permanent standard time across the United States. It repeals the temporary period for daylight saving time under the Uniform Time Act of 1966, advances standard time by one hour across standard time zones, and allows certain states and areas that were previously exempt from daylight saving time to choose either the new permanent daylight saving time or their prior standard time.
summary_detail.significance: This bill changes national timekeeping by locking the clock to daylight saving time year-round, ending the twice-yearly changing of clocks for participating jurisdictions.

title: Sunshine Protection Act of 2025
